summary: Highest legal floor in the country: the first sanctuary-state law for transgender care (SB 107, signed 2022) and shield protections against out-of-state enforcement. But also the most recorded incidents of any state in 2025 (198, GLAAD ALERT), a "dramatic increase" in Los Angeles hate-crime reports, and 34 recorded killings of trans women 2008–2025 (4.1 per 100k). Above the national score 0.36; law and street volume pull opposite ways.

sources.summary: GLAAD ALERT Desk press release (27 January 2026): 1,042 anti-LGBTQ incidents across 47 states plus DC in 2025, up 5% on 2024's 984; 51% of incidents targeted transgender and gender-nonconforming people, a 10-point increase on 2024, with June 2025 up nearly 400% since tracking began in June 2022. Per the research dossier, the desk recorded 198 incidents in California — the most of any state.

The Advocate report (27 January 2026) on the GLAAD ALERT data: 2025 was "one of the most dangerous years on record" for LGBTQ Americans, with the 1,042-incident national total and law-enforcement data showing a dramatic increase in anti-LGBTQ hate crime in Los Angeles over the same period.

The Needle investigation (16 July 2026): a state-by-state analysis of TGEU Trans Murder Monitoring killings of trans women 2008–2025 set against each state's legal-risk tier; every figure is an undercounted floor. California sits in the safest-law group yet records 34 killings (4.1 per 100k trans women/yr) — the article's headline finding is that legal risk does not predict lethal risk ("Safe States Don't Make People Safer").

KQED report (18 October 2022, updated February 2025): California became the first US "sanctuary state" for transgender youth — Governor Newsom signed SB 107 in September 2022, guaranteeing access to gender-affirming care for people coming from other states and shielding families and providers from out-of-state child-abuse investigations and criminal prosecution; the law faced opposition from conservatives and faith-based groups.

outOfScopeNotes: General crime and road-safety conditions in California are ordinary travel factors affecting everyone; they do not move trans risk.
tangentialFactors: The GLAAD incident counts cover anti-LGBTQ hostility broadly (drag events, pride disruptions as well as trans-targeted abuse), and the killing rate specifically tracks trans women — volume metrics mix adjacent categories.
localsOnly: SB 107's shields (medical-record privacy, bars on out-of-state investigations, arrests and cooperation around gender-affirming care) principally protect residents, patients, providers and families moving here; a short-term visitor invokes them only as a signal of official posture.
